previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, gastritis, and prior bladder tumor resection was admitted for chest and abdominal pain. Evaluation revealed no cardiac cause for chest pain, which resolved spontaneously, and imaging showed right lower lobe opacities consistent with pneumonia, for which oral levofloxacin was initiated. Abdominal pain was attributed to alcoholic gastritis, worsened by recent alcohol use, and managed with omeprazole and supportive care. The patient had chronic anemia with a hemoglobin of 8.1 on admission, believed to be due to multiple sources including gastritis, hematuria, and colonic angiectasias, with a low reticulocyte count suggesting inadequate red blood cell production. He was counseled on alcohol cessation and discharged home on day two with stable symptoms, instructions to follow up with primary care for anemia workup, and completion of antibiotic therapy.

************** PATIENT LEFT AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE

___ year old male with a history of HCV/ETOH cirrhosis c/b grade 
1 varices and portal hypertensive gastropathy, alcohol abuse c/b 
gastritis and EGD/Colonoscopy in ___ showing colonic 
angioectasis (treated with argon therapy) who presented with 
complaints of blood in stool and hematemesis, but subsequently 
left AMA.

# Report of BRBPR and Hematemesis: Patient presented with 
recurrent complaint of GI bleeding. Of note, his DRE did not 
reveal blood in the rectal vault (although stool guaiac was 
positive), his hematocrit was at baseline, and he was 
hemodynamically stable. Patient has a history of gastritis, 
likely exacerbated by his active drinking. He also has a history 
of colonic angioectasia s/p APC and hemorrhoids which are also 
possible etiologies of his BRBPR. His repeat hematocrit 8 hours 
later was stable. On ___, the patient insisted on LEAVING 
AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE. He verbalized his understanding that 
leaving AMA could be hazardous to his health, placing him at 
risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and death from blood loss. He 
nevertheless wished to leave and exhibited capacity to make his 
own medical decisions so he was not detained.

# Alcohol abuse: Patient has a long history of alcohol abuse and 
presented acutely intoxicated with EtOH level of 120 on 
admission. He also had positive opiates and barbiturates on 
urine tox screen. He was continued on his thiamine, folate and 
multivitamin while inpatient and monitored for alchol withdrawal 
per ___ protocol - he did not require administration of 
benzodiazepines.
